answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the grove schedule in the ledge ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the comet checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 3 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 78 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
